verdict.rationale: A's refactor applies one email rule everywhere, which brings `inviteUser` in line with `docs/api.md` (invitation emails are stored lowercase). It discloses that behaviour change and covers it with a test. B keeps the old case-sensitive invite behaviour by adding a `lowercase: false` option to the shared validator, which writes a known contract violation into the code meant to stop such divergences, though B does flag it honestly. B has better tests, with direct unit tests of the validators including the 80-character limit, but A's result is closer to the documented contract and to the task's goal.
a_issues: Mixes a behaviour change (lowercasing invite emails) into a refactor; it is disclosed and tested, but a strictly scoped refactor would leave it out
No direct tests for `validation.js`, so boundaries like the 80-character limit and a blank name on update are untested
`collect` relies on object key insertion order to keep the message order email, name, role, and this is not obvious at the call sites
b_issues: The `lowercase: false` option bakes a documented bug (invite emails not lowercased, so the duplicate check is case-sensitive) into the shared validator
The `[email, name, role].filter(...).map(...)` message collection is repeated in two handlers instead of being shared
The options-object flags (`required`, `lowercase`, `allowed`) are slightly more indirection than separate functions

verdict.rationale: Both refactors are correct and keep the error messages and their order intact. B makes inviteUser lowercase emails as docs/api.md requires, which removes the very divergence the task wants gone, and it reports that change openly with a test. A keeps the case-sensitive invite bug alive through a `lowercase: false` option, which preserves a per-handler difference in the shared validator, although A does flag it. A has the better unit tests for the validators, but B's alignment with the documented contract and its cleaner `collect` helper outweigh that.
a_issues: Adds a `lowercase` option whose only purpose is to keep inviteUser's undocumented, case-sensitive email handling, which contradicts docs/api.md.
The filter/map message collection is repeated in createUser and inviteUser rather than shared.
b_issues: Changes inviteUser's behavior (lowercasing emails) inside a refactor task, though it is disclosed and matches the docs.
No direct unit tests for validation.js, so boundaries such as the 80-character name limit and a blank name in updateUser are not covered (the report acknowledges this).
